record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometry and Topology
record.original_question: Does the 4-sphere S^4 carry a unique Einstein metric up to diffeomorphism?

evidence.quote: Settle the Euclidean no hair question: Does the four dimensional sphere have a unique Einstein metric (up to diffeomorphism)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^4$ denote the smooth 4-dimensional sphere. A Riemannian metric $g$ on a smooth manifold $M$ is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. Two metrics $g_1, g_2$ on $S^4$ are considered equivalent up to diffeomorphism if there exists a diffeomorphism $\varphi : S^4 \to S^4$ and a positive constant $c > 0$ such that $\varphi^* g_2 = c\, g_1$.

Question: Is the round (standard) metric on $S^4$ the unique Einstein metric on $S^4$, up to diffeomorphism and rescaling? Equivalently, must every Einstein metric on $S^4$ be isometric (after rescaling) to the round metric of constant sectional curvature?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of whether $S^4$ admits a unique Einstein metric (up to diffeomorphism and scaling) is a well-known long-standing open problem in 4-dimensional Riemannian geometry. Surveys by Anderson and others list it as unresolved; only partial results are known under additional hypotheses (e.g., symmetry assumptions, curvature pinching, or non-negative sectional curvature for toric/diagonal metrics).

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Einstein Metrics on 4-Manifolds (M. Anderson)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the open problem of classifying / proving uniqueness of Einstein metrics on $S^4$.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of Einstein metric on $S^4$ is highlighted as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Two open problems on S^4 with Einstein metric of positive scalar curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open problems concerning Einstein metrics of positive scalar curvature on $S^4$.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of Einstein metrics on $S^4$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Toric Einstein 4-manifolds with non-negative sectional curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes that under $T^2$-invariance and non-negative sectional curvature, Einstein metrics on $S^4$ are round.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial uniqueness results are known under symmetry/curvature hypotheses.
